methodology.summary: All four scores contribute equally. The universe is limited to companies above $2B with adequate score coverage.
paragraphs: Multi-Variable Equity Model is constructed only from the existing Stockmonk US coverage universe. Intended investment horizon: 3-5 years. Every selected company passed the strategy's sector, size, liquidity and score-coverage screens.

Eligible US-listed companies are ranked with the Stockmonk four-factor scores: Growth 25% · Quality 25% · Valuation 25% · Technical 25%. All four scores contribute equally. The universe is limited to companies above $2B with adequate score coverage.  The highest-ranked names are selected subject to a 6% single-stock cap and a 30% sector guide. Weights use score-proportional sizing. The portfolio is reviewed quarterly.

No ETF, mutual fund or non-US-listed security is eligible. Missing data is not filled with an estimate. A company without a full research report remains eligible only where the quantitative strategy calls for it, and its constituent card links to score evidence rather than a research report.
The performance shown is a current-constituent simulation, not a live track record. Rebalancing proposals are generated from the same rules and remain proposed until a future review is executed.

sections.title: Investment thesis

All four scores contribute equally. The universe is limited to companies above $2B with adequate score coverage.
Multi-Variable Equity Model is one of 105 Stockmonk model portfolios built from the same 3,696-name US coverage universe used by the screener.

sections.title: Strategy and construction
paragraphs: The selection score weights Growth 25%, Quality 25%, Valuation 25% and Technical 25%. All four scores contribute equally. The universe is limited to companies above $2B with adequate score coverage.
Eligible companies are ranked, selected up to 30 names and sized with a 6% single-stock cap. The sector guide is 30%.

sections.title: Risks and what would change the thesis
paragraphs: Large-cap factor spreads can be narrow; the portfolio may track the broad market more closely than a thematic basket.
The model is rules-based and transparent, but it cannot anticipate every macro, regulatory or company-specific shock. A factor can remain out of favour for years.
The current review proposes no changes; all holdings still meet the strategy's screening thresholds.
